summary: The one decision today, rejecting the $10 VXUS buy, looks sound on the information available. The Skeptic's point held: the proposal reversed the Market Analyst's 'prefer US core over international' call, VXUS is a beta-1.12 equity fund that adds correlated risk (Implicator: 10% stress loss from -22.84 to -23.96), and its invalidation sat about 0.9% under entry, so normal noise would trip it (L1 applied: stop must be sensible at the expected fill). At about 1.7% of equity it could not diversify anything, and it would have used the last cash above the 10% buffer before a hawkish Fed hold and the Alphabet shock. The close shows the account ended at $607.61 (+$6.98, +1.27% since start, ahead of SPY at +0.38%), about 88% invested, which meets the owner's 'mostly invested' goal, so holding the remaining cash needed little justification. The shadow portfolio (+5.4%, 99% invested) is well ahead, but that gap is mostly from earlier days and from holdings the agent never owned (RRC, CALX, TTEK), so one day of this rejection says nothing about it. Nothing was sold and no held thesis was broken by today's news. Open items: DPZ's invalidation ($274.88) is still anchored to the pre-fill reference close and sits about 13% under the $316.58 fill (L1 follow-up flagged on several prior reviews and still not re-anchored); DPZ is -1.2% on the fill and has a new securities-class-action overhang (motion to dismiss denied, derivative-claim investigation announced 10-28). IDXX prints about 11-02 and is the main event risk in the book. The account still has no ex-US exposure, which is a conscious choice given the Market Analyst's view, not an oversight.
lessons: L1 follow-up: re-anchor DPZ's invalidation to the actual $316.58 fill (about $285 for a 10% stop) at the next decision. It has been flagged for several sessions with no action, and the current $274.88 is about 13% under the fill, looser than the 10% intended.

Do not approve token-sized buys (about 1.5% of equity or less) whose only support is 'asset-class diversification' when the Market Analyst explicitly prefers the other side. Require either a size big enough to matter or an invalidation that is more than a 200-day line sitting about 1% away. Holding the cash for a better entry was the right call here.

When the cash buffer leaves almost nothing deployable, a clean reject is fine. Revisit international exposure only if the Market Analyst's view changes (VXUS 21d and 63d returns back at or above SPY) or a larger starter fits under the cash buffer.

DPZ now carries a live legal overhang plus a PT cut. It is not a broken thesis (the case rests on cash-backed quality and low beta), but a further PT cut, an adverse ruling, or cfo falling below net income should trigger a review of whether to trim.
